title: New padel courts approved despite fears for neighbouring squash club
text:

 Darren Shield Thu, 5 November 2026 at 5:00 am UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. A visualisation of the scale of the expanded tennis club with padel courts (Image: Architects Plus) Plans for a major expansion of a Carlisle tennis club have been approved despite objections from neighbouring residents and concerns that the development could threaten the long-term viability of an adjoining sports club.
 Cumberland Council has granted planning permission for two covered tennis courts, three covered padel courts and two outdoor tennis courts at Chatsworth Lawn Tennis Club on St Aidan's Road.
 The development will include two large canopy structures, reaching heights of 11.2 metres and 9.4 metres, along with new lighting and associated landscaping.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, the plans prompted objections over noise, light pollution, parking and the potential impact on neighbouring properties.
 Carlisle Squash and Racketball Club also raised serious concerns about the proposals, warning that the new padel courts could block natural light entering its gym.
 In an objection submitted on behalf of its committee, the club's chairman said: "It is great to see a local sports club increasing their offering to their members, both in the form of improved tennis facilities and the chance to play a new sport in the form of padel."
 However, the committee said changes to the original plans would leave the proposed structures too close to its building.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It said: "The long-term viability of the squash club is reliant on maintaining our large membership, especially the gym numbers, and this structure will seriously reduce the experience of our members using the gym facility."
 The committee also raised concerns about access for maintenance and the potential cost of installing additional lighting.
 It suggested reducing the number of padel courts from three to two as a compromise.
 Council considers objections
 Planning officers acknowledged that the development could affect natural light entering the neighbouring gym but concluded that this would not justify refusing permission.
 Their report stated: "The provision of natural light is not essential for the operation of the gym facility."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It added that any potential legal right to light was a civil matter rather than a material planning consideration.
 Residents of St Aidan's Road and Victoria Place also objected, raising concerns about the scale of the canopies, increased noise, flood risk and parking.
 The proposals were amended during the planning process to move the covered courts further from neighbouring homes.
 Officers concluded that the changes would sufficiently reduce the impact on residents.
 Year-round sporting facilities
 According to the applicant's Design and Access Statement, the existing outdoor tennis courts have reached the end of their serviceable life and no longer meet current competition and accessibility standards.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The new covered facilities would allow tennis and padel to be played throughout the year, while improving access for wheelchair users.
 The development is also expected to create the equivalent of one additional full-time job.
 Sport England raised no objection, concluding that the sporting benefits would outweigh the loss of an area of grassland currently used for junior rugby.
 The council approved the scheme subject to conditions, including restrictions limiting the use of covered courts to between 7am and 10pm.
 Outdoor tennis court lighting must be switched off by 9pm.
